what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/customer-follow-up: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: See where each customer is
payload.job: See where each customer is: their latest step, every step so far, and how many customers each product has against its target
payload.description: Reads the customer records you send (read them from your store): customer-contact ({contactId, displayName}), customer-product-target ({targetId, productId, productLabel, targetCount}) and customer-step ({stepId, contactId, productId, stepKind, label, createdAt}) rows, in records or as a JSON file from your files. It reads no store itself and keeps nothing. Returns each customer with their steps newest first and latest step (most recently active first), each product's customers, target, how many remain and percent, and the customer you name in contact_id (or the most recent).

records.description: The customer records, bare or as {payload}, read from your store; send this or records_file

records_file.description: A JSON file in your files (1f: then 64 hex, as find_file or list_files returns it) holding the records as a list, or as {"records": [...]}; send this or records

contact_id.description: Optional: the customer to single out

payload.label: Record a step with a customer
payload.job: Write down a step with a customer, such as outreach, a reply, a booked call, a purchase, onboarding, a follow-up or feedback, as a record
payload.description: Builds the step record, with a new id, its time, a label (a plain default for the kind when none is given), the outcome and each piece of evidence once, and returns it as step_record; it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store, where see-where-each-customer-is is given it.

contact_id.description: The customer's id, as their customer-contact record names it

product_id.description: The product the step is about

step.description: What kind of step it was

label.description: Optional: the step in a few words

evidence.description: Optional: references that show it happened (a message id, a file, a payment)

at.description: Optional: when it happened (ISO time; default now)

payload.label: Add a customer
payload.job: Add a customer or contact to my customer list, with their name, how to reach them and where they came from
payload.description: Builds the customer record and returns it with its id (contact_id, contact_record); it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store. The id is what record-a-customer-step and see-where-each-customer-is use. Give contact_id to change a customer you already added.

contact_id.description: Optional: the id of a customer you already added, to change them

reach_them_by.description: Optional: how you reach them, like Email or Instagram

came_from.description: Optional: where they came from, like a referral or an ad

record_model._what: The record kinds, indexes and links this tool keeps (moved unchanged from trillion-rust's one record model: src/record_model_policy/record-model.json, src/record_indexes/record-indexes.json, product/lists.json field_kinds and product/record-sharing.json links).

kinds._read_by: src/customer-databases.mjs: a customer-named private record database backed by its own RecordBook Durable Object

record_model._what_moved: Moved here from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid, where they were held unchanged after the engine's one record model left it (old trillion src/record-model.json and src/record-indexes.json): the kinds this tool's job keeps, each as old trillion declared it.

payload.label: Set a product's customer target
payload.job: Set how many customers I want for a product, so progress toward that target can be tracked
payload.description: Builds the target record (one per product, its id made from the product's) and returns it as target_record; it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store, replacing the earlier target of that product. see-where-each-customer-is counts the product's customers against it.

product_id.description: The product's id, as your customer steps name it

customers.description: How many customers the product aims for

active.description: Optional: false to stop tracking this target
